question: Israeli colonisation and settlements in Palestine: EU support for the International Court of Justice

The United Nations Assembly adopted in December 2022 Resolution A/RES/77/247 requesting an opinion of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Israeli practices and settlement activities affecting the rights of the Palestinian people and other Arabs of the occupied territories.

The European Union, which claims to uphold international law and human rights and deems Israeli settlements and expropriations in occupied territory to be illegal, has neither made any submissions to assist the ICJ nor submitted the regular reports from the European consuls and their delegation in Jerusalem which record these practices and other acts of Israeli violence. 1.
Why has the EEAS not assisted the International Court of Justice by submitting the information it possesses on Israel's colonisation and other acts of violence in occupied territory?
How does it intend to contribute to the International Court of Justice's opinion on the matter?
Will it submit the information in its possession to the ICJ and take part in the ICJ hearings?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.

2024) The decision to submit written statements and/or to participate in the public hearings (held between 19 and 26 February 2024) on the request for an advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in respect of the legal consequences arising from the policies and practices of Israel in the occupied Palestinian territory*, including East Jerusalem, was taken by the Member States individually and there was no decision regarding these proceedings at the level of the EU.
The EU reaffirms its continuing support to the ICJ. As the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, the ICJ has a vital role to play in the peaceful settlement of disputes.
* This designation shall not be construed as recognition of a State of Palestine and is without prejudice to the
individual positions of the Member States on this issue.
